subject: Civil Engineering
title: Equipment and Crane Operations
description: A short lesson to help you apply Equipment and Crane Operations.

hook.text: A tower crane lifts 20 tons 300 feet in the air — one wrong move and disaster follows.

buildup.text: Crane selection depends on lift capacity, reach, and site space — the wrong crane can't do the job.

discovery.text: Lift plans calculate load weight, boom length, and ground bearing — every lift is engineered.

twist.text: Wind limits crane operations — most tower cranes shut down above 20 mph gusts.

climax.text: Mobile cranes can tip over if outriggers aren't on solid ground — the most common crane accident.

punchline.text: A crane can build a skyscraper — or destroy one. Every lift is a calculated decision.

quiz.question: What is the most common cause of mobile crane accidents?
options: Lifting loads that exceed the crane's rated capacity
Outriggers not placed on solid ground, causing the crane to tip over
Operator error in swinging the boom too fast
